note: Design proposal recorded from IDEAS §1.10, 'A seal is the only warrant this package can represent' (open). Nothing here is implemented; each row is a draft proposal for a human to weigh at `nestor ui`, not a taken decision. The full argument, checked against this tree and against the two sibling repositories §1.10 cites, is docs/warrants.md. §1.10's claims about the siblings were verified before being built on: jeles' `_KIND_RANK` is `{asserted:1, machine:2, human:3}` (corpus.py:370) and `institutional` is genuinely outside it — `put_nugget` refuses any verification_kind not in that dict (corpus.py:449-452), so an institutional warrant cannot be written as a nugget kind at all and exists only on search hits with verified_by/verified_at empty (institutional.py:150). One correction to §1.10's framing, and it is the reason this memo exists: §1.10 proposes the field be called `evidence`, but it was written before the evidence edge landed (0142/0143/0145), and `nestor/evidence.py` now defines `evidence` as the thing that carries NO authority — 'there is no power to forge'. A warrant is the opposite property. The name collision would have been discovered after the schema hardened.

decisions.question: §1.10 proposes `evidence: dict` on the pair, keyed by warrant kind. Is `evidence` the right name, given the evidence edge shipped since §1.10 was written?
decisions.commitment: No — proposed name is `warrants` (nestor/warrant.py, pair['warrants'], WARRANT_KINDS), leaving the evidence edge's name, weakness and meaning untouched. Proposed shape: a table beside evidence sharing its append-only form, NOT a dict column on the pair. A dict column loses what the edge already has — a ledger line per attachment, and `attaches_to` recording which status the reference was offered against.
decisions.why: nestor/evidence.py defines its relation by the absence of authority: 'attaching a reference is not a ratification ... it carries no authority and needs none ... there is no power to forge.' A warrant is precisely a claim that DOES carry authority and IS checkable by someone who was not here. Naming both `evidence` puts two opposite properties on one word in one package — `evidence.attach()` confirming nothing, beside `pair['evidence']['citation']` whose whole purpose is to confirm something. Renaming after rows exist is the expensive case; the field does not exist yet, so it is free now.

decisions.question: Is the citation warrant a new relation, or the evidence edge extended?
decisions.commitment: Proposed: the evidence edge is most of it already, in the wrong register. `attach(pair_id, kind='url', locator=...)` records a citation today. Two things it cannot record: WHO VOUCHES (jeles carries the naming institution as a field distinct from the url; an institution written into the edge's free-text `reason` is not queryable) and HOW A STRANGER CHECKS (the edge is a pointer by design; a citation with no check procedure is a bookmark). So: not a new relation — the edge's shape plus a vouching authority and a check procedure.
decisions.why: Building a second pointer relation beside an existing pointer relation is the two-paths-into-the-store defect this repo has fixed four times (IDEAS §1.6-1.8, TODO's closing note). The difference between evidence and citation is not the pointer, it is the authority and the check — so that is what should be added, and nothing else.

decisions.question: §1.10(a): does `pending` stay the answer for a row with citation but no seal, or is 'cited, unsealed' a distinct served state?
decisions.commitment: Proposed: `pending` stays; 'cited, unsealed' is said ALONGSIDE it, never as a fourth status value. `status` means who touched the row HERE, and best_sealed's tier-1 gate is built on exactly that (`if row['status'] != 'sealed': continue`, memory.py:1126). Warrants surface on the served answer and on Passage.state's display fact (cascade.py:245), which is already separate from the stored status. best_sealed keeps gating on `sealed` alone and gains §1.10's actual ask — answering 'warranted how' — by returning the warrants of the row it found, not by widening what it will find.
decisions.why: A fourth status would put a warrant no local human vouched for into the field tier 1 reads. That is jeles' laundering case arriving by a different door — and jeles fixed that by adding a rung BELOW, never by widening what the top rung admits. The display layer already distinguishes stored status from shown state, so nothing needs inventing; the honest sentence ('nothing verified matched; say so rather than improvising') gets more useful without getting less true.

decisions.question: §1.10(b): can a `constructed` warrant be minted locally at all?
decisions.commitment: Proposed: no. A constructed warrant stores a RECIPE and an EXPECTED DIGEST — what to run, against what input, what it must produce — and Nestor never marks it satisfied. It reports 'recomputable: here is how'; the reader who cares runs it. Nestor holds the recipe and not the verdict.
decisions.why: redential-cli's warrant is worth something because the shape proves it — zero network calls PROVEN by mocking node:http/node:https/fetch at module resolution, not asserted in prose. A local process writing the string 'constructed' is an assertion wearing a proof's clothes, which is the `asserted` rung again. Holding the recipe and not the verdict is the same posture the seal already takes: the store holds the signature and does not hold the key.

decisions.question: §1.10(c): must `import` strip warrants it cannot verify, as §1.7 made import unable to revive a rejection?
decisions.commitment: Proposed rule, stronger than stripping: import may carry a warrant, and may never carry a CONCLUSION about it. By kind — attestation: unchanged, is_verified_seal already decides on import as everywhere else. Citation: carry it, marked unverified-here, because a citation's whole nature is that a stranger can follow it and stripping it destroys the only warrant that survives leaving the room. Construction: carry the recipe, never a verdict — which falls out of the previous row automatically, since there is no verdict to carry.
decisions.why: The argument is already in the tree one line above where the change would go. portable.py:80-81 says bundles carry evidence safely because 'evidence holds no authority, so unlike a pair there is nothing to sign'. Evidence rides the import path BECAUSE it is powerless. A warrant is not powerless — that is the whole distinction — so the same carriage is unsafe for it by the same reasoning. This is not an analogy to §1.7; it is the existing rule applied to a field that changes its premise.

decisions.question: Should the accumulating warrant set ever acquire an ordering?
decisions.commitment: Proposed: never, not even a convenience max() for display. §1.10 is right that 'sealed by Sean' and 'cited to Crossref' do not compare, and jeles' code settles how to act on that: it resolved the category error by SEGREGATION (the unrankable warrant lives on a different object — search hits, not nuggets). Accumulation on one object is the better answer here because segregation costs a second object per kind and makes 'sealed AND cited' unrepresentable, which §1.10 correctly identifies as the point. But jeles' precedent is why the set must stay unordered.
decisions.why: An ordering is the thing a display convenience adds by accident and a scoring path then depends on. jeles ranks only the three kinds it judges for itself and structurally refuses to write the fourth; the ranking survived an adversarial pass precisely because the unrankable kind could not enter it. Writing the constraint down before the field exists is cheaper than catching it in review — the same reasoning 0142 used for the exemption shape.
